subject: A20
question: What are VMO and MMO of the A320?
explanation: VMO 350 kt, MMO M 0.82. The VLS/VMAX strip on the PFD speed scale shows the current limits; high speed protection applies in normal law.

subject: A20
question: On the A320, what is VFE for CONF FULL?
explanation: A320 VFE: CONF 1 230 kt, CONF 1+F 215 kt, CONF 2 200 kt, CONF 3 185 kt, CONF FULL 177 kt. (Values differ on A319/A321.)

subject: A20
question: What is the maximum speed for landing gear retraction (VLO retraction) on the A320?
explanation: VLO extension 250 kt, VLO retraction 220 kt, VLE 280 kt / M 0.67.

subject: A20
question: What is the basic maximum tailwind for take-off and landing on the A320?
explanation: Basic limitation: 10 kt tailwind for take-off and landing (15 kt is available on some aircraft as an option/with specific approval). Maximum demonstrated crosswind is 38 kt gust included.

subject: A21
question: How many temperature zones are controlled on the A320?
options: 3: cockpit, forward cabin and aft cabin
4: cockpit, forward, mid and aft cabin
explanation: The zone controller regulates three zones (cockpit, FWD cabin, AFT cabin) via hot air trim valves; the packs deliver air at the temperature demanded by the coldest zone.

subject: A21
question: With the RAM AIR pushbutton ON (DITCHING not selected) and a differential pressure below 1 psi, the outflow valve (in automatic control):
explanation: RAM AIR ON opens the ram air inlet; if ΔP < 1 psi the outflow valve opens about 50 % (automatic control) to allow ventilation airflow. If ΔP ≥ 1 psi the check valve stays closed and there is no flow.

subject: A21
question: Pressing the DITCHING pushbutton closes:
options: The outflow valve, the emergency ram air inlet, the avionics ventilation inlet and extract valves, and the pack flow control valves
The engine bleed valves and the APU bleed valve
explanation: DITCHING sends a closure signal to all valves below the flotation line: outflow valve, ram air inlet, avionics ventilation inlet/extract valves and pack flow control valves.

subject: A21
question: The ECAM warning CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT is triggered when the cabin altitude exceeds:
options: 9 550 ft (or landing field elevation + 1 000 ft if higher)
explanation: EXCESS CAB ALT: cabin altitude above 9 550 ft (or landing elevation + 1 000 ft when higher, e.g. high-altitude airports). Passenger masks deploy automatically at about 14 000 ft.

subject: A22
question: After ALPHA FLOOR activation, how do you exit TOGA LK?
options: Move the thrust levers to CL
Disconnect the autothrust (instinctive disconnect pushbutton or A/THR pushbutton)
explanation: A.FLOOR commands TOGA thrust; once the angle of attack has decreased the FMA shows TOGA LK. Thrust remains locked at TOGA until A/THR is disconnected (then set thrust levers as required).

subject: A22
question: With both engines operating, autothrust is active when the thrust levers are:
explanation: A/THR is active between IDLE and CL with both engines (between IDLE and MCT with one engine). Beyond CL the A/THR is armed and the levers command thrust manually.

subject: A22
question: During an all-engines take-off, SRS mode commands a speed target of:
explanation: SRS (all engines): V2 + 10 kt. After an engine failure SRS targets the higher of V2 or the current speed (up to V2 + 15 kt), with attitude limits.

subject: A22
question: After take-off, the autopilot can be engaged at the earliest:
options: At 100 ft AGL and at least 5 s after lift-off
explanation: AP engagement is possible 5 seconds after lift-off and above 100 ft (FCOM limitation for take-off).

subject: A22
question: During an ILS approach with LOC and G/S engaged, LAND mode engages at:
explanation: LAND engages at 400 ft RA: LOC and G/S are locked (no mode change possible except go-around), followed by FLARE (~40 ft) and ROLL OUT.

subject: A24
question: What is the rating of each IDG and of the APU generator?
explanation: Each IDG and the APU generator provide 90 kVA, 115/200 V, 400 Hz. One generator can supply the whole network (with some galley load shedding).

subject: A24
question: In the emergency electrical configuration, the emergency generator is driven by:
options: The blue hydraulic system, pressurised by the RAT
explanation: After loss of AC BUS 1 and 2 above 100 kt the RAT deploys automatically and pressurises the blue system, which drives the emergency generator (CSM/G) supplying AC/DC ESS buses.

subject: A24
question: Once an IDG has been disconnected with the IDG pushbutton, it can be reconnected:
options: In flight by pressing the pushbutton again
explanation: IDG disconnection is irreversible in flight: reconnection is performed on the ground by maintenance. Do not press the pushbutton for more than 3 s.

subject: A24
question: What is the priority order for supplying AC BUS 1?
options: APU GEN, EXT PWR, GEN 1, GEN 2
GEN 1, EXT PWR, APU GEN, GEN 2
EXT PWR, GEN 1, APU GEN, GEN 2
GEN 1, GEN 2, APU GEN, EXT PWR
explanation: Each AC bus is supplied in priority by its own engine generator, then external power, then the APU generator, then the opposite engine generator (via bus tie).

subject: A24
question: The A320 has:
explanation: Two 23 Ah batteries, connected to the DC BAT bus. They also supply the static inverter (AC ESS) when the emergency generator is not available.

subject: A24
question: In emergency electrical configuration (emergency generator running), which displays remain available?
options: PFD 1, ND 1, upper ECAM (E/WD) and MCDU 1
explanation: On the emergency generator, the captain's PFD and ND, the E/WD (upper ECAM) and MCDU 1 remain powered (via AC/DC ESS). On batteries only, PFD 1 and E/WD remain.

subject: A26
question: Pushing the ENG FIRE pushbutton:
options: Silences the aural warning, arms the squibs and closes the LP fuel, hydraulic fire shut-off, engine bleed and pack flow control valves, cuts FADEC power and deactivates the IDG
Closes the cross-feed valve and starts the APU
explanation: ENG FIRE pb: silences CRC, arms the AGENT squibs, closes LP fuel valve, hydraulic fire shut-off valve, engine bleed valve and pack flow control valve, cuts off FADEC power and deactivates the IDG. Agents are discharged with the AGENT pushbuttons.

subject: A26
question: Each engine fire detection system uses two loops (A and B). A fire warning is generated when:
options: Both loops detect a fire, or one loop detects a fire while the other is faulty
Only the loop A detects a fire
explanation: The FDU uses AND logic between the two loops. If one loop is faulty, the other alone can trigger the warning. A break of both loops within 5 s also triggers a fire warning.

subject: A26
question: In case of an APU fire on the ground:
options: The crew must discharge the agent manually
The APU shuts down and the fire bottle discharges automatically
The engines are shut down automatically
explanation: On the ground the APU fire protection is automatic: APU shutdown and agent discharge (a warning also sounds in the nose gear bay). In flight the crew discharges the agent.

subject: A27
question: How many flight control computers of each type are installed on the A320?
explanation: 2 ELAC (elevator/aileron, normal pitch & roll), 3 SEC (spoilers, standby elevator and THS), 2 FAC (rudder, yaw damper, flight envelope).

subject: A27
question: In normal law with slats/flaps retracted, the load factor limitation is:
explanation: Load factor protection: +2.5 g / −1 g clean; +2 g / 0 g with slats extended.

subject: A27
question: In normal law, if the pilot releases the sidestick with a bank angle greater than 33°:
options: The aircraft rolls back to wings level
explanation: Bank angle protection: max 67° with full sidestick deflection; above 33° spiral static stability is introduced and, if the stick is released, the bank returns to 33°.

subject: A27
question: In alternate law (ALTN 1), which protection is retained?
explanation: In alternate law the load factor limitation is kept; pitch and bank attitude protections are lost and AoA / high speed protections are replaced by low speed and high speed stability.

subject: A27
question: Which PFD message indicates that the aircraft is in direct law?
explanation: In direct law, auto-trim is no longer available: the PFD displays 'USE MAN PITCH TRIM' (amber). 'MAN PITCH TRIM ONLY' (red) appears in mechanical backup.

subject: A27
question: In mechanical backup, the aircraft is controlled by:
options: The pitch trim wheel (THS) for pitch and the rudder pedals for lateral control
explanation: Mechanical backup (temporary, e.g. during total electrical loss): pitch via the THS with the trim wheels, lateral via the rudder pedals; the aim is to keep control while restoring the electrical system.

subject: A28
question: On the A320ceo, fuel transfers from the outer to the inner wing tank cells when:
options: The inner cell quantity decreases to about 750 kg
The crew selects the transfer pushbutton
explanation: Transfer valves open automatically when the inner cell reaches ~750 kg and the outer cell fuel drains by gravity to the inner cell (they latch open until the next refuelling).

subject: A28
question: In automatic mode, the centre tank pumps stop:
options: As soon as the centre tank is empty
5 minutes after the centre tank low level is reached
When the inner tanks are full
explanation: The centre tank pumps run in priority when the slats are retracted, stop when the wing tanks are full (overflow protection) and stop 5 minutes after centre tank low level is reached.

subject: A28
question: Fuel used to cool the IDG oil is returned to:
options: The outer cell of the wing tank
The engine fuel return line only
explanation: The fuel recirculation system takes fuel heated by the IDG oil cooler and returns it to the outer cell of the wing tank (its temperature is monitored).

subject: A29
question: Which hydraulic system is pressurised by the RAT?
explanation: Green: engine 1 pump. Yellow: engine 2 pump, electric pump, hand pump. Blue: electric pump and RAT. All three operate at 3 000 psi.

subject: A29
question: The PTU operates automatically when:
options: The blue system pressure is low
The differential pressure between the green and yellow systems exceeds 500 psi
explanation: The PTU transfers power (not fluid) between the green and yellow systems in either direction when ΔP > 500 psi. It is inhibited during the first engine start and during cargo door operation.

subject: A29
question: On the ground, the blue electric pump runs automatically when:
options: At least one engine is running (or BLUE PUMP OVRD is pressed)
explanation: The blue electric pump operates in flight, and on the ground when one engine is running; the BLUE PUMP OVRD pushbutton (maintenance panel) allows ground operation.

subject: A29
question: Normal braking and alternate braking are supplied respectively by:
explanation: Normal brakes: green system (with anti-skid via BSCU). Alternate brakes: yellow system, backed by the brake accumulator. The landing gear is actuated by the green system.

subject: A29
question: The cargo doors are operated by:
options: The yellow system (electric pump or hand pump)
explanation: The cargo doors are actuated by the yellow system, pressurised by its electric pump or by the hand pump. The PTU is inhibited during cargo door operation.

subject: A30
question: Wing anti-ice uses hot bleed air to heat:
options: The three outboard slats of each wing
The wing leading edge between engine and fuselage
explanation: Hot air from the pneumatic system heats the three outboard slats (3, 4, 5) of each wing.

subject: A30
question: In case of loss of electrical power to an engine anti-ice valve, the valve:
explanation: Engine anti-ice valves are electrically controlled and pneumatically operated; without electrical supply they open automatically (when air is available). Wing anti-ice valves close when electrical power is lost.

subject: A30
question: Probe and window heating operate automatically:
options: Only when the PROBE/WINDOW HEAT pushbutton is ON
When at least one engine is running (pitot at low level on the ground)
Only when the outside temperature is below 10 °C
explanation: Heating is automatic when at least one engine is running or in flight; on the ground pitot heating is at low power and the TAT probes are not heated. The pushbutton allows manual ON before engine start.

subject: A31
question: A level 3 ECAM warning is characterised by:
options: Red colour, repetitive chime (or specific aural) and flashing red MASTER WARN
explanation: Level 3 (red, MASTER WARN, CRC/specific sound): immediate action. Level 2 (amber, MASTER CAUT, single chime): awareness, action may be needed. Level 1 (amber, no aural): monitoring.

subject: A31
question: How many Display Management Computers (DMC) are installed?
explanation: EIS: 6 display units, 3 DMCs (DMC 3 can replace 1 or 2 via EIS DMC switching), 2 FWCs and 2 SDACs.

subject: A31
question: Which computers generate the warnings and cautions resulting from failures detected by aircraft systems?
options: The FWCs, using data acquired directly and through the SDACs
explanation: The SDACs acquire system data and send it to the FWCs and DMCs; the FWCs generate warnings, memos, aural alerts and radio callouts.

subject: A32
question: How is the landing gear extended by gravity?
options: By turning the gravity extension handcrank clockwise three turns
By selecting the green hydraulic system OFF
By pushing the L/G lever down twice
explanation: The handcrank (3 turns clockwise) isolates the gear hydraulics from the green system, unlocks the doors and gear, which then fall by gravity aided by aerodynamic forces.

subject: A32
question: Which autobrake mode is selected for take-off on the A320ceo?
explanation: MAX is armed for take-off (activated on a rejected take-off above 72 kt by ground spoiler extension). LO and MED are landing modes.

subject: A32
question: With the yellow system lost, the brake accumulator alone provides approximately:
explanation: The accumulator provides about 7 full brake applications (or parking brake for ≥ 12 h). Monitor the triple brake pressure indicator.

subject: A34
question: How long does a complete IR alignment take?
explanation: A complete alignment takes about 10 minutes (longer at high latitudes); a fast alignment takes about 30 seconds. The aircraft must not be moved during alignment.

subject: A34
question: Where can the crew check that GPS is used as the primary position source?
options: 'GPS PRIMARY' on the MCDU PROG page (and ND messages if lost)
explanation: The PROG page shows 'GPS PRIMARY' and the required/estimated accuracy. 'GPS PRIMARY LOST' is displayed on the ND and MCDU if integrity is lost.

subject: A35
question: Passenger oxygen masks deploy automatically when the cabin altitude exceeds:
explanation: Automatic deployment at about 14 000 ft cabin altitude; manual deployment via MASK MAN ON. Oxygen is produced by chemical generators once a mask is pulled.

subject: A36
question: Engine bleed air is normally taken from:
options: The HP stage at all times
The IP stage, the HP valve opening at low engine power
explanation: Air is normally bled from the intermediate pressure stage; at low power (e.g. descent at idle) the HP valve opens to keep sufficient pressure.

subject: A36
question: When the APU bleed valve is open, the engine bleed valves:
explanation: Engine bleed valves close automatically when the APU bleed valve is open (also for overpressure, overheat, leak, ENG FIRE pb or engine start).

subject: A36
question: With the X BLEED selector in AUTO, the crossbleed valve opens:
options: When the APU bleed valve is open
explanation: In AUTO the crossbleed valve opens when the APU bleed is used, and closes in case of wing, pylon or APU bleed leak (except during engine start).

subject: A49
question: Using the aircraft batteries only, the APU can be started up to:
explanation: Battery-only APU start is possible up to 25 000 ft; above, normal aircraft electrical supply is needed. The APU can then be used up to the maximum operating altitude.

subject: A49
question: The APU generator rating is:
explanation: The APU generator is identical in rating to the IDGs: 90 kVA, 115/200 V, 400 Hz, and can supply the whole network.

subject: A70
question: During an automatic ground start, the FADEC:
options: Uses both igniters simultaneously and cannot abort
Uses one igniter (A or B alternately) and automatically aborts in case of hot start, hung start, stall or no light-up
Requires the crew to open the HP fuel valve manually
explanation: On ground auto start, one igniter is used (alternating A/B between starts) and FADEC has full authority to abort and perform dry cranking. In flight, both igniters are used and FADEC only monitors.

subject: A70
question: For a FLEX take-off, the flexible temperature must be:
options: Higher than TREF and OAT, and not above the maximum FLEX temperature
Higher than the maximum FLEX temperature
explanation: FLX TEMP must be greater than the flat rating temperature (TREF) and OAT, and within the maximum FLEX temperature; reduction is limited to 25 % of TOGA thrust. TOGA can be selected at any time.

subject: A70
question: Each engine FADEC is:
options: A single-channel computer powered by the aircraft network only
A dual-channel computer, also powered by its own engine-driven alternator once the engine is running
explanation: FADEC: two channels (one active, one standby), mounted on the engine, supplied by its own magnetic alternator above a given N2 and by the aircraft network for start.

subject: A99
question: Unreliable speed memory items: below the thrust reduction altitude, the initial thrust/pitch is:
explanation: After AP/FD/A-THR OFF: below THR RED ALT → TOGA / 15°; above THR RED ALT and below FL100 → CLB / 10°; above FL100 → CLB / 5°. Then flaps/speedbrakes/gear as per procedure.

subject: A99
question: In response to a TCAS RA on an aircraft without AP/FD TCAS mode, the PF should:
options: Disconnect the AP, set both FDs OFF and follow the RA vertical speed green sector
Keep the AP engaged and select V/S
explanation: AP OFF, both FDs OFF, smoothly and firmly follow the RA (vertical guidance only) — never manoeuvre contrary to an RA — then notify ATC.

subject: A99
question: Which is one of the Airbus golden rules for pilots?
options: Always use the highest level of automation
Fly, navigate, communicate — in that order
Always read the ECAM before flying the aircraft
explanation: Airbus golden rules: fly, navigate, communicate (in that order); use the appropriate level of automation at all times; understand the FMA at all times; take action if things do not go as expected.

subject: A99
question: In case of a 'WINDSHEAR' reactive warning during take-off after lift-off, the crew should:
options: Retract the flaps to reduce drag
Set TOGA, follow the SRS orders (or fly up to full back stick if needed), and not change the configuration until out of windshear
Continue the climb with CLB thrust
explanation: Windshear recovery: TOGA thrust, follow SRS (up to full backstick if required — protections remain), do not change configuration, closely monitor flight path and speed, report to ATC.
